text: /untilship-dependency-upgrade Start the loop with exactly: node .untilship/bin/untilship-check.cjs start dependency-upgrade --set package=react --set target=^19 --set build="npm run build -w @helicon/ui -w @helicon/web" --set typecheck="npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p packages/ui/tsconfig.json && npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p apps/web/tsconfig.json && npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p apps/web/tsconfig.test.json" (upgrade React 18 to 19 in @helicon/ui and @helicon/web: react, react-dom, @types/react, @types/react-dom)
Single copy of React 19 now. Running the full check.
Two kinds of React 19 type errors: `RefObject` is now nullable, and the global `JSX` namespace was removed. Before fixing, I'll commit the bump and scan for other React 19 breaking APIs.
The full check passes. Committing the type fixes.

React 19 is in place in `@helicon/ui` and `@helicon/web`, and a full run of the loop's check passes: version check, the scoped build, all three type checks, and the whole `npm test` suite with 0 failures. The Stop hook makes the official check when this turn ends.

**Two commits on `untilship/r1`:**
1. **Version bump:** `react`, `react-dom`, `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` go from `^18.3.x` to `^19.2.0` in both workspaces, which installs 19.3.0. After the first `npm install`, an old React 18.3.1 copy was left at the root `node_modules`; that's the copy radix-ui, floating-ui and phosphor-icons resolve to. Running `npm dedupe` removed it, so there's now a single React 19 copy and nothing pins 18.
2. **Type fixes:** the upgrade broke three places in `packages/ui`:
   - In `Sidebar.tsx`, two props now take `RefObject<HTMLButtonElement | null>`, because `useRef(null)` returns a ref that can be null in React 19.
   - In `Toasts.tsx`, `JSX.Element` is replaced with an imported `ReactElement`, because React 19's types no longer provide a global `JSX` namespace.

I searched both packages for APIs that React 19 removed (`ReactDOM.render`, `findDOMNode`, `propTypes`, `defaultProps` on function components, string refs, `react-dom/test-utils`) and found none. The code still uses `forwardRef`, which works in React 19, so I left it alone.

`landing/` was already on React 19 and isn't a workspace, so I didn't touch it. The only uncommitted files are the loop's own `.untilship/runs/` output.
